artist.name: Sara Kays
artist.short_description: Indiana-raised singer-songwriter known for personal, narrative-led pop about relationships, self-image and growing up.
artist.biography: Sara Kays is an American singer-songwriter from Carmel, Indiana, whose songs often explore vulnerable moments with a direct, diary-like approach. She began singing young and received a guitar from her mother, then spent much of her school years performing covers on the street and at local venues. As she became more interested in writing her own material, she moved to Nashville, where she developed an ongoing recording partnership with producer Steven Martinez. Her early work includes the 2018 project A House Too Big and the 2020 EP Camera Shy. Songs such as Smaller Than This, Chosen Last and No Matter the Season brought candid subjects, including self-image and isolation, into her music. Kays used short clips on TikTok to test unfinished ideas; the response to Remember That Night? encouraged her to complete and release it quickly in November 2020. That song became her breakthrough recording and led to wider touring and television exposure. In 2021, she released Struck By Lightning on Atlantic Records, including a duet with Cavetown. Her songwriting frequently returns to everyday relationships, friendship changes and the discomfort of growing up, while allowing personal experiences to shape the stories. In January 2025, Bench Sitter began a new release chapter, followed by the seven-song Reasons To Call You project in May. For Afterglow, her catalogue offers several entry points into intimate, narrative-led emotional pop.

career_milestones.description: Released early project A House Too Big; documented as a debut EP by the Shazam artist reference.

songs.artist_statement_paraphrase: Kays said a former partner contacted her months after their breakup and brought earlier feelings back; a TikTok response led her to finish and release the song rapidly.

related_songs.explanation: Both address how romantic closeness changes after a relationship shift.
Both explore the emotional pull of memories.

related_songs.explanation: Emotional distance during a relationship versus an old breakup reopened.
